name: Coluracetam
lead: Coluracetam (also MKC-231 or BCI-540) is a racetam-class compound sold online as a nootropic. People who take it say they are after steadier mood, lower anxiety and sharper focus, which in a looksmaxxing context fits into recovery and mental-state goals that support training, sleep and a consistent routine rather than a direct change in appearance [1].

It was developed by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma, first for Alzheimer's disease, and later in-licensed by BrainCells Inc. for major depressive disorder. BrainCells announced exploratory Phase 2a results on 14 June 2010 that it said suggested potential use in major depression with comorbid generalized anxiety disorder [1][2]. It is not approved anywhere; Australia lists it as prescription-only (Schedule 4) and the FDA has not approved it [1].

Its best-described action is enhancement of high-affinity choline uptake, the rate-limiting step in acetylcholine synthesis, shown in rodent models of cholinergic deficit [1][2]. Wikipedia records anecdotal user reports of brighter colour perception, mood lift and reduced anxiety, which are not clinically established [1].

paras: Coluracetam enhances high-affinity choline uptake in rat hippocampal tissue treated with the cholinergic neurotoxin AF64A [2]. A 1994 study reported improved working memory in treated mice, a 1996 study reported improved water-maze learning in rats, and a 2007 study reported that it reversed phencyclidine-induced deficits in rats; a 2008 study reported lasting cognitive improvement after repeated dosing [1]. Later cell-line work reported that direct modulation of the choline transporter was not reproduced under basal conditions, and an AMPA receptor-related action has been suggested [2]. Wikipedia describes a structural group that is a bioisostere of the tacrine family [1].

Mitsubishi Tanabe tested it for Alzheimer's disease, where it reportedly did not reach trial endpoints [1]. BrainCells received a California Qualifying Therapeutic Discovery Program grant and in-licensed it for major depressive disorder; its exploratory Phase 2a results were announced on 14 June 2010 [1]. Grokipedia states the licence ended in 2012 and development was discontinued by 2015 [2].

A phase IIa exploratory trial under BrainCells in people with major depression and anxiety was reported to give preliminary positive signals [1][2]. Detailed peer-reviewed results were not located. No study has examined appearance outcomes.

It is sold online as a nootropic. Wikipedia records anecdotal claims of enhanced colour perception, slight synaesthesia, an "HD visual effect", better mood and reduced anxiety, citing a Russian-language source, and notes these are not clinically established [1]. It is prescription-only in Australia and unapproved by the FDA [1]. Side effects are not described in the reference sources.

card.summary: An abandoned pharma racetam sold as a nootropic, with no appearance evidence.

quick.overview:
Coluracetam is an experimental racetam developed by a Japanese drug company, tested for Alzheimer's and depression, and later sold online as a nootropic.

No source links it to appearance.
quick.mechanism: It increases choline uptake in rodent brain tissue, raising acetylcholine synthesis; AMPA-related effects have also been suggested.
quick.risks: No approved use; side-effect data are not described in the sources reviewed. Prescription-only in Australia.

chain: Raises choline uptake and acetylcholine synthesis in rodent brain tissue

Steadier mood and focus that people tie to consistent training and routine
angle.text: People take it for mood, calm and focus rather than for an appearance change. Any link to looks runs through feeling better and sticking with training, sleep and grooming habits.
